submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective layer-0 token-identity detector: it fires (about 1.3-2.8) on the current token when that token is one of a fixed set of forms, namely the 'roll' stem (' rolled', ' roll', ' rolls', ' rolling', ' roller'), ' would'/' wouldn', the contraction "'d", ' called' (not call/calls/named), and a space-prefixed single quote " '" that opens a quoted string or word (code or prose), with weaker firing (0.4-1.2) on ' tomorrow', weekday names, ' till', digits ' 7'-' 9', some first names (Robin, Roy) and Romance/Dutch function-word pieces such as Spanish ' la', ' che', ' na', ' ve'; context barely matters, near-synonyms (tossed, bounced, will, should, 'll, named, double quotes, months) stay low, and separately the first token of a text gets a positional boost (pronoun openers like She/They/It reach 1.0-1.3).

rival_explanations: Semantic reading: the pole tracks hypothetical/irrealis modality and rolling or calling events generally, so other modals (could, should, might), 'll, and synonyms like tossed, spun or named would also fire.

Quotation/opener reading: the pole is mainly a string- or quote-opening detector, so any opening delimiter (double quotes, ('), backticks) and the first token of a text would fire about as strongly as the single quote, while word tokens like rolled and would are a side effect.
